sections.normalized_html:
For a transformation

[MATH: [u; v; w]]

the Jacobian determinant of [MATH: \mathbf T,] denoted [MATH: \dfrac{\partial (x, y, z)}{\partial (u, v, w)} ,] is given by

[MATH: (∂(x, y, z))/(∂(u, v, w))|=|(∂x)/(∂u)|(∂x)/(∂v)|(∂x)/(∂w); (∂y)/(∂u)|(∂y)/(∂v)|(∂y)/(∂w); (∂z)/(∂u)|(∂z)/(∂v)|(∂z)/(∂w)|.]

First, we find the partial derivatives:

[MATH: (∂x)/(∂u)|= 2|(∂x)/(∂v)|= − 1|(∂x)/(∂w)|= 0; (∂y)/(∂u)|= 1|(∂y)/(∂v)|= 3|(∂y)/(∂w)|= 1; (∂z)/(∂u)|= 1|(∂z)/(∂v)|= 2|(∂z)/(∂w)|= − 1]

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

[MATH: (∂(x, y, z))/(∂(u, v, w))|=|2|− 1|0; 1|3|1; 1|2|− 1|; = 2|3|1; 2|− 1|− (− 1) ⋅|1|1; 1|− 1|; = 2(− 3 − 2) + (− 1 − 1); = − 10 − 2; = − 12.]
